title: Yankees re-sign Tim Hill in first of many expected bullpen moves: Sources
content:
Free-agent left-handed reliever Tim Hill and the New York Yankees have agreed to a one-year, $2.25 million contract for the 2027 season, league sources confirmed to The Athletic. The sources spoke on condition of anonymity because the deal, which also includes a $2.5 million club option for 2028, has not been completed.

Hill struggled with the Yankees in 2026. He pitched to a 4.60 ERA, the worst mark in his three seasons with the club. He was left off New York’s wild-card and American League Division Series rosters.

Hill’s return is expected to be the first of several bullpen moves for the Yankees.

“That’s probably our biggest need because we have so many vacancies of certainly important people who did a great job for us,” Brian Cashman told reporters at the general managers’ meetings in Las Vegas.

One key reason Hill struggled this season was his inflated home run-to-fly ball ratio. Over 30 percent of fly balls opposing batters hit went for home runs, by far the worst rate of his career. A team source, speaking on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly, said the Yankees expect Hill to perform better in home run suppression moving forward because other underlying metrics remained similar to his 2025 season.

Before the Yankees re-signed Hill, left-hander Brent Headrick was the only reliever under contract. They are still waiting on closer David Bednar to decide whether he will accept the qualifying offer. Even if Bednar declines the qualifying offer — the deadline is Tuesday — the Yankees still want him to return.

“He’s a cool customer,” Cashman said of Bednar. “We’ve been very lucky over the course of time, for the most part, to have somebody with a strong presence and great leadership to lead out there, and he checked all those boxes along with the performance. So I’ve had some good additions; I’ve had some not-so-good additions. He’s been a good addition so far, and hopefully we find a way to keep him so I can worry about surrounding him with more quality individuals that our manager can turn to late in the game to try to close things out.”

ESPN’s Jeff Passan first reported Hill’s contract.
